title: Maximum Sum BST in Binary Tree
summary: Given a binary tree, find the maximum sum of keys in any sub-tree that forms a Binary Search Tree.
statement: Given a binary tree, find the maximum sum of keys in any sub-tree that forms a Binary Search Tree. A Binary Search Tree is characterized by having all left descendants less than the node's value and all right descendants greater, with both left and right sub-trees also being BSTs.
constraints: A BST subtree requires every left value to be strictly smaller and every right value strictly larger recursively.
Choose any rooted subtree and maximize its node-value sum.
Return zero when every valid BST subtree has a negative sum.

editorial: Postorder recursion summarizes each subtree with validity, extrema, and sum. Infinite empty-tree bounds make leaves fit the same strict inequalities. Valid sums update a maximum initialized to zero. The oracle independently reconstructs and inspects every subtree using separate node objects.
